questions.cardText:
[Mathematics] Which of the following is topologically different from the other two?
A. A donut  B. A bowl  C. A coffee mug
Answer: B. In topology, a donut and a coffee mug are considered topologically equivalent (or homeomorphic) because they both have one hole. This concept is part of the “rubber sheet geometry” of topology, where shapes can be stretched and bent without cutting or gluing.
questions.en: In topology, which everyday drinking vessel is considered equivalent (homeomorphic) to a donut, because both have exactly one hole?
questions.de: Welches alltägliche Trinkgefäß gilt in der Topologie als gleichwertig (homöomorph) zu einem Donut, weil beide genau ein Loch haben?

timeline.labelEn: Henri Poincaré publishes Analysis Situs, a founding paper of topology; he named the notion of homeomorphism
timeline.labelDe: Henri Poincaré veröffentlicht „Analysis Situs“, eine Gründungsschrift der Topologie; von ihm stammt der Begriff Homöomorphismus

questions.notes: 'Which is different' only works among the options; asks the underlying fact from the explanation (the 'topologist's breakfast': mug = doughnut). A mug with a handle is meant.

questions.cardText:
[Astronomy] Which planet is known as the “Evening Star” due to its bright appearance?
A. Mars  B. Jupiter  C. Venus
Answer: C. Venus is called the “Evening Star” when it is visible after sunset and the “Morning Star” when it appears before sunrise.
questions.en: Which planet is known as the "Evening Star" when it shines brightly after sunset, and the "Morning Star" before sunrise?
questions.de: Welcher Planet wird „Abendstern“ genannt, wenn er nach Sonnenuntergang hell leuchtet, und „Morgenstern“ vor Sonnenaufgang?

timeline.labelEn: The Babylonian Venus tablet of Ammisaduqa, the oldest known record of Venus's positions
timeline.labelDe: Die babylonische Venustafel des Ammi-saduqa, die älteste bekannte Aufzeichnung der Positionen der Venus
